Synopsis

StepSecurity confirmed synckit 0.11.9 as one of the npm packages affected by the July 2025 npnjs.com maintainer phishing campaign. The attacker used a phished maintainer credential path to publish malicious releases directly to npm without corresponding source repository changes.

Story

synckit was one of the smaller packages in the npnjs.com phishing wave. Its importance comes from campaign linkage: a stolen maintainer credential let the attacker publish directly to npm under the legitimate package name.

Version 0.11.9 was the malicious release. Like the Prettier tooling packages in the same wave, it was distributed through npm without a corresponding normal source change, so consumers saw a registry event before they saw a repository event.

The package belonged to the JavaScript tooling ecosystem, where install hooks run in developer and CI environments. Even a small package can matter when it is transitive and executes before application code starts.

The campaign record carries the broader phishing infrastructure. This record keeps the artifact-level coordinate, version, and npm distribution path separate.
